about: Voice lines, screenplay v3; times assumed from a calm read until the scratch read.

lines.text: A handful of sand. Hardly a treasure.
Depends what you find.
Come along. There’s something remarkable inside quartz.
Many sand grains contain quartz. For this journey, we start with selected quartz rock.
What am I made of?
Silicon and oxygen, joined in a crystal.
In a fiercely hot furnace, carbon helps remove the oxygen.
Oh! We’re going different ways.
We have silicon. But it isn’t pure enough yet.
We convert it into a chemical that’s easier to purify.
Distillation separates it from unwanted substances.
Another reaction deposits very pure silicon onto heated rods.
Next, we melt the purified silicon.
A seed crystal touches the melt, then slowly rises and turns.
Silicon solidifies onto it, following the seed’s atomic pattern.
All that… is me?
One continuous crystal. An ingot.
The ingot is sliced into thin discs.
Their surfaces are finished, polished, and carefully cleaned.
Am I a chip now?
A wafer. We’ll build many chips on you.
Welcome to the fab. Precious cargo coming through!
Here we build the circuits. Even a speck of dust can spoil the work.
First, we add a thin film of material.
Then a light-sensitive coating, called photoresist.
Light transfers a pattern. Developing opens selected parts of the coating.
Etching removes material through those openings.
Adding selected atoms changes how parts of the silicon conduct electricity.
Clean. Measure. Check.
Again?
Many times. Each step has a job.
Together, these steps build transistors and their connections.
One wafer. Many chips, called dies.
Inside, transistors control electrical signals: tiny switches working together.
Electrical probes test the dies while they’re still on the wafer.
Did I pass?
You passed.
We cut along the spaces between the dies.
Where to now?
A package protects the die and connects it to the outside world.
So I can join in.
One final test. Then the chip can become part of a device.
From quartz to silicon. From wafer to working chip.
Quite a lot inside something so small.
